hints: Focus only on the two ends that join to make a peptide bond, the NH2 group on one amino acid and the COOH group on the other. Ignore the H atoms on the central carbon (2 and 5).
Remember condensation means water is made as OH from a carboxyl group plus H from an amino group. Check which numbered H atoms sit in those two exact places.
walkthrough:
**Find the reacting groups**

Look at each amino acid. Each has an amino group ($-NH_2$) on the left and a carboxyl group ($-COOH$) on the right.

A peptide bond always forms between C of one COOH and N of the other $NH_2$. The H atoms on the middle carbon, 2 and 5, never take part.

**Recall how water is made**

This is a condensation reaction. You remove $OH$ from the carboxyl group and $H$ from the amino group.

Together they make water:
$$OH + H \rightarrow H_2O$$

**Match this to the numbers**

In one possible joining, the left amino acid provides the $NH_2$ and the right amino acid provides the $COOH$.

That means H atom 1 from the left $-NH_2$ plus the H atom 6 from the right $-OH$ combine with oxygen to make water. That is option B.

options.A: Both 1 and 4 are H atoms on amino ($-NH_2$) groups. You need one H from an amino group and one H from a carboxyl OH group, so two amines cannot make water.
options.B: Atom 1 is an H from an amino group and atom 6 is the H from a carboxyl OH group. OH + H makes $H_2O$ during condensation to form the C-N peptide bond.
options.C: Atom 3 is from a carboxyl OH which is correct, but atom 5 is on the central alpha carbon and is never removed when a peptide bond forms.
options.D: Atom 4 is from an amino group which is correct, but atom 2 is on the central alpha carbon and stays in the dipeptide, so it cannot be part of water.
